recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is recommended for this issue unless a future work-group decision reopens the modifier-extension update rule.
issue_request: FHIR-18361 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked to clarify that systems are not barred from updating unrelated parts of a resource merely because another part contains an unknown modifier extension; the final rule applies when the resource as a whole or the element being modified has child modifier extensions the system does not understand, or when the modified element is a descendant of an element containing such modifier extensions.
initial_application: Upstream commit 9cee2b12d67a79dc05b7176be66fb200fad24fa8 changed source/extensibility.html from the old broad 'contains modifier extensions' wording to the Jira-approved scoped wording, and git blame still attributes the current rule to that commit.
additional_context: source/extensibility.html is in build scope through source/fhir.ini's active type-page entry extension=extensibility. The latest combined branch preserves the approved wording. Nearby published Jira issues FHIR-17699 and FHIR-6160 are earlier/background modifier-extension clarifications, and the neighboring FHIR-18362 reconciliation did not alter the FHIR-18361 rule. Zulip and Confluence searches found no directly relevant conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current active source already satisfies FHIR-18361.
